newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan prices seen easing as interest weak.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan prices seen easing as interest weak.

text.p: A lack of speculative interest amid a dearth of market-moving factors and weaker prices in producing countries are expected to drag yen-based rubber futures lower next week, rubber traders said on Friday.

Overnight news that the Kuala Lumpur-based International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) is set to resume rubber market intervention to stabilise prices, has failed to arouse investor interest, traders said.

"The market was starved of fresh factors and trading has been very dull. News about INRO has not had much of an impact on the market as the planned intervention price level is below current prices," one analyst at a commodity broker said.
Benchmark November on the Tokyo Commodities Exchange (TOCOM) ended Friday morning at 134.0 yen per kg, against Thursday's close of 133.5 yen.
Benchmark November on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 134.4 yen per kg, up from 134.1 yen on Thursday.

"Sentiment in rubber futures is very bearish due to a lack of investor interest. Open interest of rubber futures has fallen continously as investors are shifting money away to more volatile commodities," another commodity broker analyst said.
Despite the yen's dive against the dollar on Thursday, there was little fresh buying, which indicates how bearish the market is, he said.
Trade in yen-based commodity futures is usually given a boost by fluctuations in the currency market.
Open interest of TOCOM rubber futures was 113,479 lots as of Thursday, down from 132,316 lots on May 1 and 172,616 as of January 29.
One trader said TOCOM benchmark November would test the downside of 132.0 yen next week, and that stop-loss selling could emerge if prices were not supported at that level.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 116.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Friday, down from 118.00 U.S. cents on June 6.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 148 yen as of Friday, compared with 149 yen on June 6.
